comments.body: I like that the paper treats Bell-state availability as something the compiler has to budget, not as a network detail that magically works out later. That makes the remote CNOT cost model feel closer to the actual distributed-machine constraint.

score_assessment.rationale: Specific, grounded in the paper's remote-CNOT and Bell-state constraints, and adds a clear interpretation.

comments.body: The one-data-qubit-per-QPU line topology is a harsh model, but that harshness is useful. It keeps the linear bounds from being oversold as average behavior on richer quantum-network topologies.

score_assessment.rationale: Accurately frames the restrictive architecture as a conservative analytical choice without overstating results.

comments.body: The data-qubit-swapping result seems especially relevant for circuits with repeated interaction patterns. If moving the data once helps several later CNOT layers, the n/4-style bound is not just a better constant but a hint about workload structure.

score_assessment.rationale: Connects the theorem and repeated interaction patterns to a practical compiler-design implication.

comments.body: That comparison with the hypercube-based compiler needs careful reading. A method tuned for a line network is solving a different problem than one that can assume much more favorable connectivity.

score_assessment.rationale: Useful reply that reinforces the topology caveat from the experiments, though it is less detailed than the root comments.

comments.body: The O(dn2) distribution complexity is an important part of the contribution for me. It signals that the authors are not chasing optimal distributed compilation, but a scalable heuristic with analytically bounded overhead.

score_assessment.rationale: Highlights the implementation complexity and correctly situates it against impractical optimal compilation.
